question: Was Abraham justified by faith or works?
summary: Paul and James pick the same proof text — Genesis 15:6 — and push it in opposite directions. Romans 4:2 explicitly says Abraham was not justified by works. James 2:21 explicitly says Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac. Two New Testament writers using one Old Testament figure to make incompatible soteriological claims.

reconcile.connective: Gill meets the two verses directly, distinguishing Paul's justification before God from James's justification before men — works as cause versus works as evidence.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the flat opposition: Romans 4:2 denies Abraham was justified by works; James 2:21 affirms he was, over the same episode.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: …but does not the Apostle James say that he was justified by works, Jam 2:21? To this it may be replied, that the two apostles, Paul and James, are not speaking of the same thing: Paul speaks of justification before God, James of justification before men; Paul speaks of the justification of the person, James of the justification of a man's cause, as the truth of his faith, or the uprightness of his conduct; Paul speaks of works, as the causes of justification, James of them as the effects and evidences of faith; Paul had to do with the self-righteous, who trusted in their own works for justification, James with Gnostics, who slighted and neglected the performance of them. These things considered, they will be found to agree.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill names both verses explicitly (Rom 4:2 and Jam 2:21) and states the exact reconciling move used across the harmonizing tradition — before-God/before-men, cause/evidence — the single tightest, most self-contained on-tension statement across the six voices. Leading ellipsis marks the trim from Gill's preceding exposition of Rom 4:2; the excerpt ends on a real source period.
excerpts.source_note_text:
For if Abraham were justified by works,.... That Abraham was not, and could not be justified by works, is clear from hence, that if this was his case,
he hath whereof to glory; which will be allowed him before men, on account of his pious life and conversation:
but not before God; who saw all the iniquity of his heart, and was privy to all his failings and infirmities: besides, glorying before God in a man's own works, is contrary to the scheme and method of God's grace; is excluded by the doctrine of faith; nor is there any place for glorying before God but in Christ, and his righteousness: if therefore Abraham had not that of which he could glory before God, he could not be justified by works in his sight: but does not the Apostle James say that he was justified by works, Jam 2:21? To this it may be replied, that the two apostles, Paul and James, are not speaking of the same thing: Paul speaks of justification before God, James of justification before men; Paul speaks of the justification of the person, James of the justification of a man's cause, as the truth of his faith, or the uprightness of his conduct; Paul speaks of works, as the causes of justification, James of them as the effects and evidences of faith; Paul had to do with the self-righteous, who trusted in their own works for justification, James with Gnostics, who slighted and neglected the performance of them. These things considered, they will be found to agree.
